podcast.title: Recruitment into Velvet Revolver (2003)
podcast.body: Dave Kushner, formerly of the band Wasted Youth, was convinced by Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum to join their new band, Velvet Revolver, as they sought a singer. "Plus they had convinced their buddy Dave Kushner for a band called Wasted Youth to join up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Outsider Perception at Press Conference (2004)
podcast.body: At a press conference for Velvet Revolver's "Contraband" album, Dave Kushner appeared quiet and likely felt like an "outsider," contrasting with the more integrated demeanor of the other members. "Dave Kushner was quiet, probably feeling like a bit of an outsider."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dave Kushner Joins Velvet Revolver (2003)
xref.body: Dave Kushner, formerly a member of Wasted Youth, was recruited into the supergroup Velvet Revolver by the ex-Guns N' Roses members. "Plus they had convinced their buddy Dave Kushner for a band called Wasted Youth to join up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation as a Supergroup (2003)
xref.body: Formed in 2003, Velvet Revolver began with former Guns N' Roses members Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum, who then recruited Dave Kushner from Wasted Youth. They auditioned several singers, including Josh Todd of Buckcherry, Travis Meeks of Days of the New, and B-Real of Cypress Hill, before settling on Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Former Members Form Velvet Revolver (2003)
xref.body: Three former members of Guns N' Roses – Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum – reconciled and formed a new band, Velvet Revolver, in 2003, eventually recruiting Dave Kushner and Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band. It was Duff, Slash, and drummer Matt Sorom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Velvet Revolver Audition and Trust (2003)
xref.body: Scott Weiland initially disliked the music sent by the future Velvet Revolver members but agreed to jam after hearing a second, improved CD. Despite arriving hours late due to drug use, he found the chemistry with Duff McKagan, Slash, Matt Sorum, and Dave Kushner to be "bang on" and trusted Matt Sorum from a shared rehab experience. "Besides, he'd been in rehab with Matt Sorom so he trusted him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Velvet Revolver Formation (2003)
xref.body: After reconciling with Slash and Matt Sorum, Duff McKagan was one of the three core Guns N' Roses members who initiated the formation of Velvet Revolver, eventually recruiting Dave Kushner and Scott Weiland. "It was Duff, Slash, and drummer Matt Sorom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tense Press Conference Dynamics (2004)
xref.body: At a press conference for the "Contraband" album, the former Guns N' Roses members (Duff, Slash, Matt) were friendly and engaging, while Dave Kushner was quiet. Scott Weiland, however, was totally separate, aloof, and unapproachable, creating palpable tension and doubt about the band's longevity. "He exhibited an aloofness that resulted in a puppable tension when he was in the room. And while the rest of the band was only too happy to talk, Wyland was icy cold and completely unapproachable."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
